383	        self.path = path

388	            event_hooks={"request": [self.on_request], "response": [self.on_response]},

393	            f.write(json.dumps({"t": round(time.time(), 3), **entry}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

396	        """Which headers were sent, never what the secret ones said."""
397	        out = {}
398	        for name, value in headers.items():
399	            name = name.lower()
400	            out[name] = "<redacted>" if name in SECRET_HEADERS else value

403	    async def on_request(self, request: Any) -> None:
404	        """Every attempt the SDK makes, headers and body included; the key is never written."""
405	        self.attempts += 1

407	            body = request.content.decode("utf-8", "replace")
408	        except Exception:  # a streamed body has nothing to record
409	            body = ""
410	        self._write(
411	            dir="request",
412	            method=request.method,
413	            url=str(request.url),
414	            status=None,
415	            headers=self._headers(request.headers),
416	            body=body,

420	        """The answer to it, read in full so the body is there even when the SDK streams."""
421	        await response.aread()

425	            method=req.method,

379	class Wire:
380	    """The raw HTTP record: one line per attempt, request and response, with no secret in it."""
381	
382	    def __init__(self, path: Path, transport: Any = None):
383	        self.path = path
384	        self.attempts = 0
385	        path.touch()
386	        self.client = httpx2.AsyncClient(
387	            transport=transport,
388	            event_hooks={"request": [self.on_request], "response": [self.on_response]},
389	        )
390	
391	    def _write(self, **entry: Any) -> None:
392	        with self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
393	            f.write(json.dumps({"t": round(time.time(), 3), **entry}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
394	
395	    def _headers(self, headers: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
396	        """Which headers were sent, never what the secret ones said."""
397	        out = {}
398	        for name, value in headers.items():
399	            name = name.lower()
400	            out[name] = "<redacted>" if name in SECRET_HEADERS else value
401	        return out

403	    async def on_request(self, request: Any) -> None:
404	        """Every attempt the SDK makes, headers and body included; the key is never written."""
405	        self.attempts += 1
406	        try:
407	            body = request.content.decode("utf-8", "replace")
408	        except Exception:  # a streamed body has nothing to record
409	            body = ""
410	        self._write(
411	            dir="request",
412	            method=request.method,
413	            url=str(request.url),
414	            status=None,
415	            headers=self._headers(request.headers),
416	            body=body,
417	        )

419	    async def on_response(self, response: Any) -> None:
420	        """The answer to it, read in full so the body is there even when the SDK streams."""
421	        await response.aread()
422	        req = response.request
423	        self._write(
424	            dir="response",
425	            method=req.method,
426	            url=str(req.url),
427	            status=response.status_code,
428	            headers=self._headers(response.headers),
429	            body=response.text,

128	class Plane:
129	    """The execution plane: what the model can do to the world, and the record of it."""
130	
131	    def __init__(self, root: Path, run_dir: Path, hidden: tuple[str, ...] = HIDDEN,
132	                 protected: tuple[str, ...] = PROTECTED, sandbox: Any = None):  # fmt: skip
133	        self.root = root.resolve()
134	        self.run_dir = run_dir
135	        self.hidden = hidden
136	        self.protected = protected
137	        self.sandbox = sandbox
138	        self.listed: list[str] = []
139	        self.read_paths: list[str] = []
140	        self.lines_read = 0
141	        self.written: list[str] = []
142	        self.edited: list[str] = []

145	    def _resolve(self, path: str) -> tuple[Path, str]:
146	        p = (self.root / (path or ".")).resolve()
147	        if p != self.root and self.root not in p.parents:
148	            raise ValueError(f"outside the world: {path}")
149	        rel = p.relative_to(self.root).as_posix() or "."
150	        if rel.split("/", 1)[0] in self.hidden:
151	            raise ValueError(f"not part of the world: {path}")
152	        return p, rel
153	
154	    def _writable(self, rel: str) -> None:
155	        """The goal's tests and the toolchain are the human's; the builder may read them only."""
156	        name = rel.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
157	        for pattern in self.protected:
158	            if pattern.endswith("/"):  # anything under that directory
159	                hit = rel == pattern[:-1] or rel.startswith(pattern)
160	            elif "*" in pattern:  # that basename, anywhere in the world
161	                hit = fnmatch.fnmatchcase(name, pattern)
162	            else:  # that exact path at the root, not the basename anywhere
163	                hit = rel == pattern
164	            if hit:
165	                raise ValueError(
166	                    f"protected: {rel} (the goal's tests and the toolchain are not the "
167	                    "builder's to change)"
168	                )

170	    def _capped(self) -> str:
171	        if len(self.written) + len(self.edited) >= WRITE_CAP:
172	            return f"error: cap reached ({WRITE_CAP} writes and edits); report now"
173	        return ""

175	    def list(self, path: str = ".") -> str:
176	        """List one directory of the world: one entry per line as kind, size, path. Path is
177	        relative to the world root; '.' is the root.
178	
179	        Args:
180	            path: The directory to list, relative to the world root.
181	        """
182	        try:
183	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
184	            if not p.is_dir():
185	                raise ValueError(f"not a directory: {path}")
186	            entries = sorted(p.iterdir(), key=lambda e: (not e.is_dir(), e.name))
187	            if rel == ".":
188	                entries = [e for e in entries if e.name not in self.hidden]
189	            lines = []
190	            for e in entries[:LIST_CAP]:
191	                kind = "link" if e.is_symlink() else "dir" if e.is_dir() else "file"
192	                size = e.lstat().st_size if kind == "file" else 0
193	                lines.append(f"{kind}\t{size}\t{e.relative_to(self.root).as_posix()}")
194	            if len(entries) > LIST_CAP:
195	                lines.append(f"...\t{len(entries) - LIST_CAP} more entries not shown")
196	        except (ValueError, OSError, RuntimeError) as e:  # RuntimeError: a symlink loop
197	            return f"error: {e}"
198	        self.listed.append(rel)
199	        return "\n".join(lines) or "(empty)"

201	    def read(self, path: str, start: int = 1) -> str:
202	        """Read a file of the world as numbered lines, from line `start` (1-based), at most 300
203	        lines or 32000 bytes per call; a truncated read says where to continue.
204	
205	        Args:
206	            path: The file to read, relative to the world root.
207	            start: The first line to read, 1-based.
208	        """
209	        try:
210	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
211	            if not p.is_file():
212	                raise ValueError(f"not a file: {path}")
213	            start = max(1, int(start))
214	            out: list[str] = []
215	            n = nbytes = 0
216	            with p.open("r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
217	                for i, line in enumerate(f, 1):
218	                    if i < start:
219	                        continue
220	                    size = len(line.encode())
221	                    if n >= READ_LINES_CAP or nbytes + size > READ_BYTES_CAP:
222	                        if n:  # one line per call at least, or a long line dead-ends the read
223	                            out.append(f"...\ttruncated; continue with start={i}")
224	                            break
225	                        cut = line.encode()[:READ_BYTES_CAP].decode("utf-8", "ignore")
226	                        out.append(f"{i}\t{cut} …(line cut at {READ_BYTES_CAP} bytes)")
227	                    else:
228	                        out.append(f"{i}\t{line.rstrip(chr(10))}")
229	                    n += 1
230	                    nbytes += size
231	        except (ValueError, OSError, RuntimeError) as e:  # RuntimeError: a symlink loop
232	            return f"error: {e}"
233	        self.read_paths.append(rel)
234	        self.lines_read += n
235	        return "\n".join(out) or "(empty)"

237	    def write(self, path: str, content: str) -> str:
238	        """Write a file of the world: create it, or replace what is there with `content`.

317	class Sandbox:
318	    """Where the world's tests run: a container, no network, the world mounted read-only.
319	
320	    The only place that knows about Docker. The image is the world's own locked dependencies,
321	    built once per (uv.lock, check.Dockerfile) pair and reused by every run afterwards.
322	    """
323	
324	    @staticmethod
325	    def image(world: Path) -> str:
326	        """The image name for this world: what it locks and how it is built, hashed."""
327	        h = hashlib.sha256((world / "uv.lock").read_bytes() + (world / "check.Dockerfile").read_bytes())
328	        return f"factory-check:{h.hexdigest()[:12]}"
329	
330	    @staticmethod
331	    def ensure_image(world: Path, run_dir: Path) -> str:
332	        """Build the image if it is not there yet; the build is the one step with network."""
333	        name = Sandbox.image(world)
334	        seen = subprocess.run(["docker", "image", "inspect", name], capture_output=True)
335	        if seen.returncode == 0:
336	            return name
337	        built = subprocess.run(
338	            # -f absolute: docker resolves a relative -f against the caller's directory, and the
339	            # factory never runs from inside the world.
340	            ["docker", "build", "-f", str(world / "check.Dockerfile"), "-t", name, str(world)],
341	            capture_output=True,
342	            timeout=IMAGE_TIMEOUT,
343	        )
344	        (run_dir / "image-build.log").write_bytes(built.stdout + built.stderr)
345	        if built.returncode != 0:
346	            raise RuntimeError(f"docker build failed (exit {built.returncode}); see image-build.log")
347	        return name
348	
349	    @staticmethod
350	    def run(world: Path, run_dir: Path, n: int) -> tuple[int, str]:
351	        """The world's tests, once: the exit code and everything the run printed."""
352	        name = Sandbox.ensure_image(world, run_dir)
353	        container = f"factory-check-{run_dir.name}-{n}"
354	        argv = [
355	            "docker", "run", "--rm", "--name", container,
356	            "--network", "none",  # the check cannot reach the key, the provider or the internet
357	            "--user", f"{os.getuid()}:{os.getgid()}",
358	            "-e", "HOME=/tmp",
359	            "-e", "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1",  # the world is read-only; do not try to cache
360	            "-v", f"{world}:/w:ro", "-w", "/w",
361	            "--memory", "1g", "--cpus", "2", "--pids-limit", "256",
362	            name, *CHECK_CMD,
363	        ]  # fmt: skip
364	        try:
365	            done = subprocess.run(argv, capture_output=True, timeout=CHECK_TIMEOUT)
366	        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
367	            try:  # the check is over either way; a wedged daemon must not hang the run too
368	                subprocess.run(["docker", "kill", container], capture_output=True, timeout=30)
369	            except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
370	                pass
371	            return 124, f"timeout after {CHECK_TIMEOUT} s"
372	        # unittest writes to stderr; the world's own code may write to either.
373	        return done.returncode, (done.stdout + done.stderr).decode("utf-8", "replace")

379	class Wire:
380	    """The raw HTTP record: one line per attempt, request and response, with no secret in it."""
381	
382	    def __init__(self, path: Path, transport: Any = None):
383	        self.path = path
384	        self.attempts = 0
385	        path.touch()
386	        self.client = httpx2.AsyncClient(
387	            transport=transport,
388	            event_hooks={"request": [self.on_request], "response": [self.on_response]},
389	        )
390	
391	    def _write(self, **entry: Any) -> None:
392	        with self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
393	            f.write(json.dumps({"t": round(time.time(), 3), **entry}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
394	
395	    def _headers(self, headers: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
396	        """Which headers were sent, never what the secret ones said."""
397	        out = {}
398	        for name, value in headers.items():
399	            name = name.lower()
400	            out[name] = "<redacted>" if name in SECRET_HEADERS else value
401	        return out
402	
403	    async def on_request(self, request: Any) -> None:
404	        """Every attempt the SDK makes, headers and body included; the key is never written."""
405	        self.attempts += 1
406	        try:
407	            body = request.content.decode("utf-8", "replace")
408	        except Exception:  # a streamed body has nothing to record
409	            body = ""
410	        self._write(
411	            dir="request",
412	            method=request.method,
413	            url=str(request.url),
414	            status=None,
415	            headers=self._headers(request.headers),
416	            body=body,
417	        )
418	
419	    async def on_response(self, response: Any) -> None:
420	        """The answer to it, read in full so the body is there even when the SDK streams."""
421	        await response.aread()
422	        req = response.request
423	        self._write(
424	            dir="response",
425	            method=req.method,
426	            url=str(req.url),
427	            status=response.status_code,
428	            headers=self._headers(response.headers),
429	            body=response.text,
430	        )

434	# so for `deepseek-flash` the library believes thinking is off and forces a tool choice, which the
435	# API rejects with 400 "Thinking mode does not support this tool_choice". Saying what the model is
436	# — thinking-capable, thinking on by default, no forced tool choice while it thinks — makes the
437	# library send `tool_choice: auto` and leaves thinking at the API default, as in v0.1.

445	def build_agent(
446	    plane: Plane, key: str = "", http_client: Any = None, model: Any = None
447	) -> Agent[None, BuildReport]:
448	    """The agent: the role, the five functions of the plane, a typed report, our caps."""
449	    if model is None:
450	        model = OpenAIChatModel(
451	            MODEL, provider=DeepSeekProvider(api_key=key, http_client=http_client), profile=PROFILE
452	        )
453	    return Agent(
454	        model,
455	        instructions=ROLE,
456	        output_type=BuildReport,
457	        tools=[
458	            Tool(plane.list, takes_ctx=False),
459	            Tool(plane.read, takes_ctx=False),
460	            Tool(plane.write, takes_ctx=False),
461	            Tool(plane.edit, takes_ctx=False),
462	            Tool(plane.check, takes_ctx=False),
463	        ],
464	        # No temperature: DeepSeek ignores it in thinking mode, and the settings should say what
465	        # the request actually is. Thinking stays at the API default.
466	        model_settings=OpenAIChatModelSettings(timeout=180),
467	        retries={"tools": 1, "output": 2},
468	    )

471	def run(agent: Agent[None, BuildReport], goal: str) -> tuple[BuildReport | None, list, RunUsage, str, str]:
472	    """One run under the caps: the report if there is one, the messages either way."""
473	    usage = RunUsage()
474	    report, stopped, detail = None, "answer", ""
475	    with capture_run_messages() as messages:
476	        try:
477	            result = agent.run_sync(
478	                goal,
479	                usage=usage,
480	                usage_limits=UsageLimits(tool_calls_limit=TOOL_CALLS_CAP, request_limit=REQUEST_CAP),
481	            )
482	            report = result.output
483	        except UsageLimitExceeded as e:
484	            stopped, detail = "cap", str(e)
485	        except (UnexpectedModelBehavior, ModelAPIError) as e:  # ModelHTTPError is one of these
486	            stopped, detail = "error", str(e)
487	    return report, list(messages), usage, stopped, detail
